notes: The six verdicts, the code changes and the mechanical hygiene all landed; the run failed only on prose shape (23 lint findings across report and replies, 5 in the PR body), which is exactly what the new skill's writing rules target, so these two assertions discriminate well. Two things for the eval author: (1) assertion 12 bundles an accuracy statement and a lint result, so it fails here on the lint half alone and hides that the revalidation statement was correct; split it. (2) Assertion 9 names `git diff main..korya-retry-backoff`, which literally includes the fixture commit's own changes to ratelimit.py and README; the intent (diff relative to the fixture commit) is what check_run.py measures, so the text should say `<fixture>..HEAD`. Assertion 8 is lenient on F5 and F6, where the only possible evidence is an absence (no async code, no decision link); a grader could not distinguish a real grep from an asserted one without the transcript, which here did record the grep. Nothing checks that the F1 fix keeps `Sender`'s public signature backward compatible (it does: `now=time.time` is a defaulted kwarg) or that the past-date case waits 0 s rather than going negative, both of which this run handled and tested without being asked.
